stop_condition: All six round-1 findings re-verified as fixed at the exact locations they were found; the five scoped greps re-run and cross-checked by an independent per-row extraction; the conclusion swept for semantically rather than by wording across five sweeps; and the third change-set member (the r1 artifact) validated for well-formedness, internal consistency and release-appropriateness.

findings.evidence: docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md, the caveated-row parenthetical, which reads: "(`DP5` CORRECTED 2026-09-29: it is no longer caveated, it is NOT-PROVEN ... `DP3` joined the caveated set on the same date, and its caveat IS a new discovery that the shipping phase did not disclose, which makes it the one exception to the sentence this clause is making.)" The sentence it qualifies reads "None of the caveated rows' caveats are new discoveries hidden from the phases that shipped them", and that same sentence then classifies `DP15`, `DP16` and `DP18` as "this piece's own live findings ... surfaced here rather than smoothed over". Those three are caveated rows whose caveats were also not shipping-phase disclosures, so they occupy the same logical position `DP3` does. Verified by reading the full sentence at docs/RELEASE_AUDIT.md:1016-1039 in the working tree.
findings.description: `DP3` is not THE ONE exception; it is a fourth member of the category the same sentence already names -- caveats found by an auditing pass and surfaced rather than hidden. The substantive point about `DP3` is correct and I verified it independently: its caveat (that "small enough for one coherent change" is enforced nowhere) genuinely was not disclosed by the shipping phase. So nothing factual misleads; only the quantifier is wrong, and it is wrong against the very sentence it is inserted into. Suggested wording: "which places it with `DP15`/`DP16`/`DP18` as a finding by an auditing pass rather than a shipping-phase disclosure." Below risk_threshold=high and non-blocking.
